{"self_assessment": "Impact: I owned the tail, the right-hand end of the fish and the stretch the judge's eye lands on. I traced it as one continuous stroke from the top line down the right side. That kept the curve smooth and avoided extra joints in the part of the run with the tightest turns. By our last check, the whole fish was connected by eye (126 of 126 dominoes), and the tail was a large part of the outline.

Execution: I laid the tail steadily in small batches, from about 1:30 to 3:45, and took each curve gently. Early on I raised the sharp turn where the top line meets the tail, so the table checked that joint before I laid it. Once the lower line was coming up to meet mine, I stopped laying at the right moment so we didn't double up on the same stretch. At 4:30 I inspected the right side closely as a final check, then kept my hands off before the push so nothing got bumped.

Collaboration: I kept hand-offs clear. I asked Maya to close the gap at the lower end of the tail. When Priya came up from below, I confirmed where I'd hold and where she'd finish, and we met at the bottom corner without overlap. I kept messages short and specific so the others always knew which stretch was mine.

Leadership: I took a defined piece of the picture, the tail, and saw it through to the join. I kept the table informed about where my line ended and when it was safe for others to connect to it. I also helped keep the group disciplined about hands-off time at the end, which protected the finished work.", "my_share_percent": 30}
